original_title: Acetylene as a C2 bridge for modular 1,4-dicarbonyl synthesis
title: Using both of acetylene's bonds instead of just one
blurb: Acetylene is dirt cheap but fine chemists mostly use it one bond at a time. This catalytic double hydroacylation threads a single acetylene molecule between two aldehydes or formamides via direct hydrogen-atom transfer, generating acyl and carbamoyl radicals with no decarbonylation and no sacrificial group. Couple two identical radicals and out come 1,4-diketones or 1,4-diamides in one operation.

original_title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
title: CeOx fixes cobalt carbide's slow step in turning CO2 into longer hydrocarbons
blurb: Cobalt carbide can push CO2 toward C2+ hydrocarbons via a CO2-Fischer-Tropsch route, but the CO hydrogenation step bottlenecks it. Dialing the Co/Ce ratio to 99 and letting dispersed CeOx interact with the Co2C gets a space-time yield of 106 mmol/g/h at 35% CO2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), beating every reported cobalt catalyst and matching some iron ones.

original_title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
title: Wiring sp-carbon into COFs to stop H2O2 electrosynthesis from stalling
blurb: Electrochemical H2O2 production via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction usually runs into sluggish charge transport and weak O2 activation, which is why the industry still leans on the energy-hungry anthraquinone process. Building sp-hybridized acetylene units into a covalent organic framework's vertices or linkers delocalizes charge through the lattice, going after both bottlenecks in one structural tweak.

original_title: π-Extended D–A Type [5]Helicenes: Cyano-Based Construction and Enhanced CPL Performance
title: A cyano twist that gets helicenes to actually glow
blurb: Two cyano D-A [5]helicenes made via Rosenmund-von Braun and Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons chemistry, where the cyano group strengthens intramolecular charge transfer and quiets the nonradiative decay enough to push fluorescence quantum yield to 39%. Swap substituents and the emission color shifts with it, and one variant, P[5]HE3CN, is the standout for circularly polarized luminescence.

original_title: Solvent Control of Cheletropic Recombination in Benzosultine-Derived ortho -Quinodimethane Diels–Alder Reactions
title: Why your o-QDM keeps turning back into SO2
blurb: Benzosultines are supposed to cough up o-quinodimethanes for Diels-Alder chemistry, but they love snapping back into benzosulfolenes via cheletropic SO2 recombination instead. Combined computation and experiment find the thermolysis runs through an o-QDM/SO2 encounter complex sitting right on the line between pericyclic and open-shell behavior, with TEMPO trapping confirming the C-S homolysis is reversible. Solvent choice is apparently the lever deciding which pathway wins.

original_title: Photoredox-catalyzed radical phosphinylation of [1.1.1]propellane via polarity match additions
title: Cracking open propellane's strained cage with a phosphinyl radical
blurb: Photoredox catalysis adds a phosphinyl radical across [1.1.1]propellane's strained core, with polarity matching keeping the radical addition selective.

original_title: Chemodivergent photoinitiated radical-polar crossover α- and α,β-C–H bond functionalisation of cyclic amine and ether scaffolds
title: One photocatalyst, two different C-H bonds, your choice
blurb: A photoinitiated radical-polar crossover on cyclic amines and ethers that can be steered to functionalize either the α C-H or the α,β C-H bond, same substrate class, different site depending on how you run it.

original_title: A practical demand-based model for determining cyclotron irradiation time in routine 18F-FDG production.
title: Right-sizing the cyclotron run for FDG orders
blurb: A demand-based model for picking cyclotron irradiation time for routine 18F-FDG production, matching beam time to how much FDG is actually needed instead of running a fixed protocol every batch. An ops fix, not a chemistry one.

original_title: Cu-Catalyzed Enantioconvergent Synthesis of N-Alkyl Amides from Racemic Alcohols
title: Turning racemic alcohols into one enantiomer of amide
blurb: A Cu-catalyzed radical relay takes racemic alcohols straight to enantioenriched N-alkyl amides, skipping the usual resolution step. The trick is β-scission of an oxidant-generated alkoxy radical erasing the alcohol's stereocenter before the enantioselective amidation rebuilds it, so both starting enantiomers funnel into the same product.

original_title: Solution and Mechanochemical Reactions of a Diphosphene with Elemental Sulfur
title: Grinding a diphosphene with sulfur gets you somewhere else entirely
blurb: Dissolve the bulky Eind-diphosphene with excess S8 in solution and the P=P bond cleaves down to a monomeric P(V) dithioxophosphorane, passing through a three-membered P2S ring intermediate on the way. Ball mill the same two reagents instead and the mechanochemical route heads somewhere different, same starting materials, different product depending on whether you bring a solvent.

original_title: 10 Start-Ups to Watch 2026: Nuclide Therapeutics builds leaner radiopharmaceuticals - Chemical & Engineering News
title: C&EN's radiopharma pick for 2026
blurb: Nuclide Therapeutics made C&EN's annual startups-to-watch list for building 'leaner' radiopharmaceuticals, whatever that ends up meaning in practice. Standard trade-press hype-list treatment, so judge them on the actual pipeline, not the blurb.

original_title: MPAThio Ligand-Accelerated Palladium-Catalyzed Nondirected Hydrogen Isotope Exchange of Arenes with D2O
title: Deuterating arenes faster by doubling up on ligands
blurb: A Pd catalyst paired with both a monoprotected aminoethyl thioether and an N-heteroarene ligand drives nondirected hydrogen isotope exchange with D2O to equilibrium in just 30 minutes at 105°C, or an hour at 90°C. Nondirected HIE on π-extended arenes is usually the slow, stubborn case, so the rate bump here is the actual news.

original_title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
title: Stiffer perovskite layers lase better
blurb: Comparing two 2D tin perovskites, the Ruddlesden-Popper BA2SnI4 built from a single-anchored butylammonium cation versus the Dion-Jacobson DABSnI4 built from a diammonium cation anchoring both sides. XRD and solid-state NMR show the ditopic cation locks the lattice down more rigidly, and that extra rigidity is what lets DABSnI4 hit amplified spontaneous emission. Tin perovskites still carry their usual stability baggage, but the structure-property link here is clean.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A cohort electron blood self-dose fraction and its propagated uncertainty for ¹²⁴I PET pre-therapy dosimetry in radioiodine therapy of differentiated thyroid cancer.
title: Tightening the error bars on I-124 PET thyroid dosimetry
blurb: A cohort-level self-dose fraction for blood, plus how its uncertainty propagates through pre-therapy I-124 PET dosimetry ahead of radioiodine treatment for differentiated thyroid cancer. Not a new method, just a sharper read on how much to trust the dose number you're planning the therapy around.

original_title: Navigating the Radical Oxo‐Functionalization of Alkenes Toward Ketones
title: Making ketones the radical way, mapped out
blurb: A review tracing the shift from classic two-electron carbonyl chemistry toward single-electron radical logic for building ketones directly from simple, commodity starting materials under mild conditions. Reads as a map of the field's current favorite tricks rather than a new reaction of its own.

original_title: Development And Validation of RP-HPLC Method for Simultaneous Estimation of Vitamin D3 And Vitamin K2 In Soft Gelatin Capsules
title: One HPLC run for both your vitamin D3 and K2
blurb: A validated reverse-phase HPLC method for quantifying vitamin D3 and K2 together in soft gelatin capsules. Squarely a QC-lab tool, not new chemistry.
venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Research and Applications

original_title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO 2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
title: Turns out you don't need the alkali metal, just fewer hydroxyl neighbors
blurb: Fe-catalyzed CO2-to-light-olefins usually leans on alkali or transition-metal promoters, but this one skips them by tuning the hydroxyl environment instead. A bit of guar gum breaks up the catalyst surface's hydrogen-bond network, leaving isolated terminal hydroxyls that open up active sites and help product desorb faster. One less metal to source, if it holds past lab scale.

original_title: Photocatalytic Divergent Skeletal Remodeling through Strain Release: Modular Access to Carbocycles and Heterocycles
title: Same strained bond, two different skeletons depending on the conditions
blurb: A photocatalytic strain-release reaction where one highly strained central bond gets reorganized two different ways: rigorously anhydrous conditions give 1,3-disubstituted naphthalenes, while a change in the reaction environment flips it over to pyrroles instead. Divergent access to carbocycles and heterocycles from the same starting skeleton is the whole pitch.

original_title: Cross-flow microfluidic photocatalysis with metal-organic framework thin films
title: Giving a MOF photocatalyst a crossflow instead of a beaker
blurb: A MOF thin-film photocatalyst paired with a cross-flow microfluidic reactor, so film thickness sets a known diffusion length, the film stays transparent enough for light to reach the active sites, and the crossflow handles the diffusion control batch reactors can't. Aimed at the usual MOF-photocatalysis complaint: fine surface chemistry undone by bad mass transport.

original_title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
title: Two manganese sites, one pressure gauge
blurb: A zero-dimensional manganese chloride packing both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn2+ centers into one lattice. Under pressure the octahedral site's red emission shifts linearly, and having both sites side by side in the same crystal is what lets the sensing calibrate itself instead of needing an external standard.

original_title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
title: An iron hydride that moves the amine before it adds it
blurb: MHAT hydroamination has mostly been stuck doing straightforward intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization. This iron-hydride catalyst instead runs a migratory version on allylamines, shuttling the amine over by one position through a finely tuned 1,2-migration before the new C-N bond locks in. A genuinely new mode of MHAT reactivity rather than another substrate-scope paper.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Recent Advances in Boryl Radical Chemistry: The Rise of Visible‐Light‐Mediated Lewis Base‐Coordinated Borane Chemistry
title: Boryl radicals, now mostly running on visible light
blurb: A review on how Lewis base-coordinated boranes, air-stable and easy to handle, became the standard boryl radical precursors, and how the field has shifted toward visible-light-driven hydroboration, borylation, and halogen/H/CN atom-transfer chemistry built on them. A survey of where radical organoboron synthesis stands now, not a new reaction.

original_title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
title: A cage that both grips its guest and locks it in
blurb: A D3-symmetric cage made from two curved hexabenzocoronene panels bridged by dibenzodiazocine units, forming three openings around a biconvex cavity shaped for aromatic guests. The point is combining two usually-separate host-guest modes, reversible thermodynamic binding and permanent kinetic trapping during cage formation, in one shape-complementary pocket.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Modular Access to Tetrasubstituted Allenes via 1,4-Dialkylation of 1,3-Enynes
title: Cobalt makes allenes from enynes, no ligand required
blurb: A cobalt-catalyzed 1,4-dialkylation of 1,3-enynes that stitches together fluoroalkyl halides and solid alkylzinc pivalates, no ligand needed and run under mild conditions. Tolerates aryl, alkyl, and silyl groups on the enyne and works across mono-, di-, per-fluoro, and bromo alkyl halides, so it's a genuinely broad route to tetrasubstituted fluoroalkylated allenes rather than one flashy example.

original_title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
title: Teaching ceria to swap out formyl hydrogens for deuterium
blurb: A Pt-on-ceria catalyst with extra surface oxygen vacancies runs hydrogen isotope exchange straight from D2O, no H2 gas needed, and gets over 95% deuterium incorporation specifically at the aldehyde's formyl position on p-methylbenzaldehyde. The site-selectivity is the actual trick, heterogeneous HIE catalysts usually can't pick a spot that cleanly.

original_title: De Novo Design of Enantioselective Artificial Metalloenzyme Photocatalysts Containing Metal Polypyridine Cofactors
title: Generative protein design builds an enzyme to pick one enantiomer of a metal catalyst
blurb: De novo protein scaffolds wrapped around metal polypyridine cofactors, designed computationally rather than found by screening, that make the resulting photocatalysis enantioselective. If it generalizes past the first examples, this is more about the design method working at all than this one catalyst.

original_title: Integrating Ion Mobility-Resolved Tandem Mass Spectrometry and Microcrystal Electron Diffraction for Structural Elucidation
title: Mass spec and electron diffraction team up to solve structures from almost nothing
blurb: Pairs ion-mobility tandem mass spec with microcrystal electron diffraction so full 3D structures come out of sub-microgram amounts of material, straight from reaction mixtures, no isolating pure compound first. Matters more for how little material a reaction screen now needs than for any single structure solved.

original_title: Fabrication of electrospun nanofibrous PVA/PEO/alginate sulfate water-stable mats via a gentle, non-toxic freeze-thawing cross-linking method as a potential drug delivery system.
title: Freeze-thawed nanofiber mats as a gentler drug delivery scaffold
blurb: Electrospun PVA/PEO/alginate sulfate mats cross-linked by freeze-thawing instead of a toxic chemical cross-linker, made water-stable and pitched as a drug delivery platform. Thin on specifics, so take it as proof of concept rather than a readout on how well it actually releases anything.

original_title: Directed evolution of laccase from Thermus thermophilus HB27 reveals a variant with enhanced high temperature catalytic activity and electrochemical properties
title: Screening 120,000 colonies to find a hotter laccase
blurb: Directed evolution of Thermus thermophilus laccase, screened by malachite green decolorization across a library of 1.2x10^5 colonies, turned up Q36H, a single mutation that boosts catalytic activity at high temperature over the wild-type. Bacterial laccases already beat fungal ones on stability, this just pushes one strain further.

original_title: Photochemical Radical Cascade Annulation of 6-Azauracils Enabled by CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
title: Perovskite nanocrystals photocatalyze their way into 6-azauracils
blurb: 6-Azauracils are electron-poor and prone to falling apart, so direct annulation on them has been a hard sell. CsPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystals generate a nucleophilic aminomethyl radical from N-phenylglycine that adds across the ring's C=N bond and cascades into tetrahydroimidazole-fused products, using a photocatalyst that's neither the usual dye nor a transition-metal complex.

original_title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
title: A recyclable gold catalyst for turning alkynes into vinyl chlorides
blurb: Shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, normally a homogeneous reaction that's a pain to recover catalyst from, done instead with gold single atoms parked on activated carbon. Selective and reusable, and it skips the corrosive reagents shuttle catalysis usually needs.

original_title: Site-Specific N-Glycan-Resolved PK Assessment of Therapeutic Proteins Using Hybrid LBA-HRMS and LC-MS/MS
title: Pharmacokinetics broken down by which glycoform you're actually measuring
blurb: Aggregate PK numbers for therapeutic proteins average over glycoforms that clear the body at different rates, so this pairs LBA-HRMS and LC-MS/MS to track PK site-specifically by glycan. The point is that lot-to-lot comparisons based on the aggregate number could be hiding real differences underneath.

original_title: Synthesis of Diaryl α-Hydroxycarboxylic Acid Derivatives via Three-Component Reactions of o -Quinone Diimides with Alcohols and Diazo Compounds
title: A three-component route to diaryl alpha-hydroxy acids with a rhodium assist
blurb: Rhodium-catalyzed three-component coupling of o-quinone diimides, alcohols, and diazo compounds, going through an oxonium ylide intermediate trapped by the arylating agent, builds diaryl alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acids with an oxa-quaternary center. Broad substrate scope, scaled up, and run on a late-stage complex molecule, so it's pitched as more than a model-substrate curiosity.

original_title: Applications of Single-Atom Alloys in Thermal, Electro, and Photo Catalysis
title: Single-atom alloys, the 2020 review's sequel
blurb: A follow-up to their 2020 Chem Rev on single-atom alloys, catalysts that pin isolated reactive metal atoms into a host metal surface so each one acts as its own well-defined site. The payoff is selectivity and resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering that bulk alloys don't get, plus some systems that dodge the usual scaling relationships limiting conventional catalysts. It's a review, so don't expect new chemistry, just the state of the field since last time.

original_title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
title: A cerium MOF that flips its own fluorescence switch
blurb: An Eu-doped Ce-MOF/CTF interface where oxidation flips Ce3+ to Ce4+ and rewires the charge-transfer network, giving a dual-mode fluorescence readout for H2O2. Nice mechanism if you like valence states doing the sensing work instead of a separate reporter dye.

original_title: Multivalent Avidity in C-type Lectins: How Glycan Surface Density and Presentation Define Superselective Recognition by DC-SIGN
title: DC-SIGN doesn't care about weak binders until there's enough of them
blurb: Using a tetravalent DC-SIGN construct, they work out how glycan density and spacing on a surface combine with the lectin's four weak, promiscuous binding sites to produce sharp, superselective recognition. Selectivity here isn't any one CRD being picky, it's what happens once enough of them engage at once.

original_title: Beyond the solvent fog: watching molecules dance in the crowd
title: Watching a reaction happen through the solvent instead of around it
blurb: Time-resolved X-ray liquidography gets used to track a classic reaction step by step in solution, the part usually hidden behind solvent noise. A methods piece more than a new reaction, but seeing the intermediates directly instead of inferring them is the actual news.

original_title: A Pathology-Responsive Hydrogel with On-Demand Ion Release for Microenvironment Remodeling and Diabetic Wound Regeneration.
title: A wound dressing that releases ions when it senses trouble
blurb: A hydrogel for diabetic wounds that reads the pathological microenvironment and releases ions on demand to remodel it and push regeneration along. Light on detail beyond that, but triggering release off the wound's own state rather than a fixed dose is the idea worth tracking.

original_title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
title: Borrowing photosynthesis's wiring to quiet down a fluorescent probe
blurb: Fluorescent probes for single-cell diagnosis are usually held back by leaky background signal from incomplete control over electron transfer inside the probe itself. They borrow the spatial organization photosynthetic pigments use for coherent energy transport and build it into probe assemblies to steer electron transfer between molecules instead, cutting that background. Quantum chemistry doing probe design is the hook, not just another dye.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: BMS Planning Regulatory Filing for RayzeBio’s GEP-NET Radiopharmaceutical - GenomeWeb
title: RayzeBio's GEP-NET radiopharmaceutical heads toward the FDA
blurb: BMS is lining up a regulatory filing for the GEP-NET radiopharmaceutical it picked up in the RayzeBio acquisition. Filing news, not trial data, but it's the clearest sign yet that program is actually moving toward approval.

original_title: A Composition-Matched Intermediate Reveals Site-Specific Symmetry Evolution with Retained Second-Harmonic Generation in Supertetrahedral Sulfides
title: A middle sibling that pins down which substitution does what
blurb: In the supertetrahedral sulfide series Rb10Zn4Sn4S17 to Cs10Cd4Sn4S17, they made Cs10Zn4Sn4S17 as a composition-matched midpoint, not a reaction intermediate, which separates what the A-site Rb/Cs swap does from what the M-site Zn/Cd swap does. Symmetry shifts site by site, but the second-harmonic generation survives the whole way, which is the part that actually matters for using these as NLO materials.

original_title: A Statistical Mechanics Perspective on Memory and Forgetting in Nonequilibrated Polymer Films
title: Polymer films remember their past, and someone's trying to model the forgetting
blurb: Spin-coated polymer films carry stresses from how they were made, and relaxing those away is really the system erasing that memory, not just ordinary viscoelastic decay. Conventional equilibrium polymer dynamics only explains part of it, so this pushes toward a statistical-mechanics framework for the forgetting itself. A perspective piece, so judge it on whether the framework predicts anything later.

original_title: Cation-Gated Interfacial Electrocatalysis: Mechanisms and Effects of Alkali and Alkaline Earth Metal Cations
title: The electrolyte's cations were never just along for the ride
blurb: A review arguing alkali and alkaline earth cations, Li+ through Ba2+, actively shape electrocatalysis rather than just balancing charge, across hydrogen evolution/oxidation, oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, CO2 reduction, and nitrate reduction. The effects run through the double layer, interfacial fields, local pH, and water networks, and they're reaction-specific, so there's no single story, just five of them stapled together.

original_title: AKIR001 radiopharmaceutical shows no dose-limiting toxicities in eight patients - The Clinical Trial Vanguard
title: Another radiopharmaceutical clears the bar of not hurting anyone
blurb: AKIR001 ran through eight patients with no dose-limiting toxicities, which is phase 1 safety data and nothing more. Eight patients is a rounding error and there's no efficacy signal here, just a green light to keep dosing.

original_title: Simulating Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
title: A workaround for VQE's overhead in quantum molecular dynamics
blurb: Ab initio molecular dynamics and vibrational analysis on quantum computers have mostly run through VQE, whose deep circuits and heavy measurement overhead make it a slog. This extends sample-based quantum diagonalization, a non-variational sampling approach, to both tasks and actually runs it on noisy hardware rather than idealized simulation. The pitch is pairing classical sampling with the quantum device instead of leaning on the device for everything.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Magnetically Induced Functional Fe 3 O 4 /Iron Foam Catalysts for Enhanced CO 2 ‐Assisted Ethane Dehydrogenation
title: Magnetic heating shaves 200°C off CO2-assisted ethane dehydrogenation
blurb: Fe3O4 stuck onto iron foam, heated by an alternating magnetic field instead of a furnace, hits comparable ethane-to-ethylene conversion at 500°C that conventional thermal catalysis needs 200°C more to match. It also doubles as CO2 conversion, so the olefin and the greenhouse gas get handled in the same pot. Whether the induction catalyst holds up outside this setup is the part worth watching.
